Triage (triage seat, hourly round 2026-08-26, session `session_01PVUQHLY6uhGUCs4mD9fzFC`): graded `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Bug, `domain:ui`. Same construction defect the #6489 / #6240 family already ruled, in the sibling page — verified still present on `origin/main` (`MetadataObjectsPage.tsx:182-189`): delete-detection reads `!nextByName[name]` off a plain object literal, so an object legally named `constructor` (or `__proto__`) is never detected as deleted — silent no-op, save reports success, object survives reload. Inherit the family fix (build via `Object.fromEntries` / read own-properties, or a `Map` — the card is right that a never-serialised lookup is the natural `Map` case). Fence per the card: this page's writes are per-object, so #6489's nameless/duplicate **refusals do not port unchanged** — the dev fixes the lookup keying under the inherited ruling, and if refusal semantics seem needed here, that is a fork to report, not to pick silently. Serial note: sibling file `MetadataFieldsPage` was just rewritten by merged PR #6520; no open PR holds `MetadataObjectsPage.tsx` at grading time.

### Triage's ruling, verbatim — note the fence in its second half

> Same construction defect the #6489 / #6240 family already ruled, in the sibling page — verified still present on `origin/main` (`MetadataObjectsPage.tsx:182-189`): delete-detection reads `!nextByName[name]` off a plain object literal, so an object legally named `constructor` (or `__proto__`) is never detected as deleted — silent no-op, save reports success, object survives reload. Inherit the family fix (build via `Object.fromEntries` / read own-properties, or a `Map` — the card is right that a never-serialised lookup is the natural `Map` case). Fence per the card: this page's writes are per-object, so #6489's nameless/duplicate **refusals do not port unchanged** — the dev fixes the lookup keying under the inherited ruling, and if refusal semantics seem needed here, that is a fork to report, not to pick silently.

⛔ Read that fence twice. #6489 landed **three** things: own-property keying, plus refusals for nameless and duplicate fields. **Only the first ports.** This page writes per-object, so the refusal semantics are a different question — if you come to believe they are needed here, **report it, do not pick it**.

### Premise re-verified on `origin/main` before dispatch

```
:182   const nextByName: Record<string, ObjectDefinition> = {};
:183   for (const o of next) nextByName[o.name] = o;
:189   if (!nextByName[name]) {
:191     await client.reset('object', name);
```

So a deletion of an object named `constructor` reads as "still present" and `client.reset` never fires. Silent no-op, save reports success, object survives reload.

### ⭐ A second site triage did not name — measure it, then say which it is

`MetadataObjectsPage.tsx:146` carries `byName[item.name] = item` — the same construction, in a different function. Triage's ruling names `182-189` only.

Do **not** silently fix it and do **not** silently skip it. Measure whether it is the same defect (what reads that lookup, and can a prototype-reachable name reach it?), then either fix it under the same ruling and say so explicitly, or state why it is not the same case. A card that fixes one of two identical constructions in one file, without mentioning the second, is how the next card gets filed.

### The model is now on `main`

PR #6520 landed the sibling `MetadataFieldsPage.tsx` an hour ago — it uses `Object.fromEntries` and reads the previous value with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...)`. Read it as the family model. Triage's note that a never-serialised lookup is the natural `Map` case is worth taking seriously: `nextByName` is built, read, and discarded, so unlike the fields map it never has to survive `JSON.stringify`.

### ⛔ Fixture trap — this bit the family already

**`{ __proto__: v }` in an object literal SETS THE PROTOTYPE** (Annex B.3.1); it does not add a key. A fixture written that way has zero own keys and passes for the wrong reason. Spell it `['__proto__']`, a computed key. This is not hypothetical — a pin in this exact family asserted the blind form, was filed as #6524, and my own earlier dispatch order told a dev to copy it. The corrected form and a test that pins the rule itself are now on `main` at `MetadataFieldsPage.fieldsMapKeying.test.tsx:257`–`:267`. Use that as your model.

Note also that `JSON.parse` **does** define an own `__proto__` property — so assertions on parsed bytes read honestly while assertions on literals do not.

### File face

`packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataObjectsPage.tsx`, its existing suite `MetadataObjectsPage.specKeyGroup.test.tsx`, any pin you add, and a changeset.

⛔ **Do not touch `MetadataFieldsPage.tsx`.** It is the subject of an open ungraded card (#6527, retired-key list unification) and is not yours to reshape.

### In-flight, do not touch

#6515 · #6329 (PR #6536) · #6317 · #6496, plus open PR #6533. Measured disjoint from your face against each branch's **merge base** — `packages/plugin-designer/` is touched by none of them.

Reverse verification required: the pin written first and observed failing against the untouched tree, with the failure being the *silent no-op* (an object that should have been deleted surviving), not merely a shape assertion. Prove the mutation on disk rather than trusting an editor's exit code.
